Answer: A
Reason: A lung hernia is characterized by the protrusion of lung parenchyma through a defect in the thoracic cage, appearing as an air-containing structure continuous with the intrathoracic lung; Option A correctly describes this key radiographic feature (air-density structure continuous with lung parenchyma), whereas the other options describe findings inconsistent with a herniated lung (e.g., absence of air or solid masses).
